entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12322"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 7</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Hos.7.1-Hos.7.16">Ho 7:1-16</reference>. Reproof of Israel.</title> <div sID="gen22492" type="x-p"/> Probably delivered in the interreign and civil war at Pekah's death; for <reference osisRef="Hos.7.7">Ho 7:7</reference>, "all their kings ... fallen," refers to the murder of Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, and Pekah. In <reference osisRef="Hos.7.8">Ho 7:8</reference> the reference seems to be to Menahem's payment of tribute to Pul, in order to secure himself in the usurped throne, also to Pekah's league with Rezin of Syria, and to Hoshea's connection with Assyria during the interregnum at Pekah's death [Maurer].<div eID="gen22492" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22493" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12322"/><hi type="bold">1. Political, as well as moral, healing is meant. When I would have healed Israel in its calamitous state, then their iniquity was discovered to be so great as to preclude hope of recovery. Then he enumerates their wickedness: "The thief cometh in (indoors stealthily), and the troop of robbers spoileth without" (out-of-doors with open violence). <div eID="gen22493" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12327"/><div sID="gen22504" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12327"/><hi type="bold">6. they have made ready--</hi>rather, "they make their heart approach," namely their king, in going to drink with him.<div eID="gen22504" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22505" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">like an oven--</hi>following out the image in <reference osisRef="Hos.7.4">Ho 7:4</reference>. As it conceals the lighted fire all night while the baker sleeps but in the morning burns as a flaming fire, so they brood mischief in their hearts while conscience is lulled asleep, and their wicked designs wait only for a fair occasion to break forth [Horsley]. Their heart is the oven, their baker the ringleader of the plot. In <reference osisRef="Hos.7.7">Ho 7:7</reference> their plots appear, namely, the intestine disturbances and murders of one king after another, after Jeroboam II. <div eID="gen22505" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12332"/><div sID="gen22518" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12332"/><hi type="bold">11. like a silly dove--</hi>a bird proverbial for simplicity: easily deceived.<div eID="gen22518" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22519" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">without heart--</hi>that is, understanding.<div eID="gen22519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22520" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">call to Egypt--</hi>Israel lying between the two great rival empires Egypt and Assyria, sought each by turns to help her against the other. As this prophecy was written in the reign of Hoshea, the allusion is probably to the alliance with So or Sabacho II (of which a record has been found on the clay cylindrical seals in Koyunjik), which ended in the overthrow of Hoshea and the deportation of Israel (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.17.3-2Kgs.17.6">2Ki 17:3-6</reference>). As the dove betrays its foolishness by fleeing in alarm from its nest only to fall into the net of the fowler, so Israel, though warned that foreign alliances would be their ruin, rushed into them. <div eID="gen22520" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12335"/><div sID="gen22528" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12335"/><hi type="bold">14. not cried unto me--</hi>but unto other gods [Maurer], (<reference osisRef="Job.35.9">Job 35:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Job.35.10">10</reference>). Or, they did indeed cry unto Me, but not "with their heart": answering to "lies," <reference osisRef="Hos.7.13">Ho 7:13</reference> (see on <reference osisRef="Hos.7.13">Ho 7:13</reference>).<div eID="gen22528" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22529" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">when they howled upon their beds--</hi>sleepless with anxiety; image of deep affliction. Their cry is termed "howling," as it is the cry of anguish, not the cry of repentance and faith.<div eID="gen22529" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22530" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">assemble ... for corn, &c.--</hi>namely in the temples of their idols, to obtain from them a good harvest and vintage, instead of coming to Me, the true Giver of these (<reference osisRef="Hos.2.5">Ho 2:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.8.12">8, 12</reference>), proving that their cry to God was "not with their heart."<div eID="gen22530" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22531" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rebel against me--</hi>literally, "withdraw themselves against Me," that is, not only withdraw from Me, but also rebel against Me. <div eID="gen22531" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 14. not cried unto me-- but unto other gods [Maurer], ( Job 35:9 , 10 ). Or, they did indeed cry unto Me, but not "with their heart": answering to "lies," Ho 7:13 (see on Ho 7:13 ). when they howled upon their beds-- sleepless with anxiety; image of deep affliction. Their cry is termed "howling," as it is the cry of anguish, not the cry of repentance and faith. assemble ... for corn, &c.-- namely in the temples of their idols, to obtain from them a good harvest and vintage, instead of coming to Me, the true Giver of these ( Ho 2:5 , 8, 12 ), proving that their cry to God was "not with their heart." rebel against me-- literally, "withdraw themselves against Me," that is, not only withdraw from Me, but also rebel against Me.

entries.content_plain: 16. return, but not to the Most High-- or, "to one who is not the Most High," one very different from Him, a stock or a stone. So the Septuagint. deceitful bow-- ( Psa 78:57 ). A bow which, from its faulty construction, shoots wide of the mark. So Israel pretends to seek God, but turns aside to idols. for the rage of their tongue-- their boast of safety from Egyptian aid, and their "lies" ( Ho 7:13 ), whereby they pretended to serve God, while worshipping idols; also their perverse defense for their idolatries and blasphemies against God and His prophets ( Psa 73:9 ; 120:2 , 3 ). their derision in ... Egypt-- Their "fall" shall be the subject of "derision" to Egypt, to whom they had applied for help ( Ho 9:3 , 6 ; 2Ki 17:4 ).
